public_rationale: The speaker said only that the $100 tier 'appears to have' immediately cut Plus limits, so only that factual appearance is tested, not causation. On launch day, April 9, 2026, OpenAI announced that it was 'rebalancing' Codex usage in Plus to support more sessions across the week 'instead of longer sessions in a single day' (e1, e2). That is a same-day change that cuts how much a $20 subscriber can use in one session or day, which is the reduction he described. OpenAI called it a rebalance, did not publish numbers, and may have kept or raised weekly totals. So the claim holds for short-window limits, and it is unclear whether total weekly usage fell.
limitations: No official before-and-after Plus limit figures.
The weekly allowance may not have fallen. The finding rests on the single-day and per-session window.
Causation is not assessed, in line with the speaker's hedge.

our_interpretation: The speaker hedges with 'appears to have'. He does not firmly claim that the new tier caused a cut. The checkable core is narrower: when the $100 tier launched, OpenAI changed ChatGPT Plus ($20) limits in a way that cut how much a Plus user could use, in at least one usage window. That is the 'appearance' he describes.
Causation is not tested. Only the timing link (the change came with the launch) is checked.
'Rate limits' is read as the Codex usage limits, which the launch announcement changed. That includes the short-window, per-session limits a user hits during a working session.
Target period: the launch on 2026-04-09 through the post date, 2026-04-14.
criteria.support_condition: Holds if OpenAI announced or documented a change at the $100 launch that reduced Plus users' Codex usage in at least one window, for example shorter sessions or less use in a single day.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Fails if Plus limits stayed the same or rose in every window at the launch, or if OpenAI made no Plus change at that time.
